question.worked_solution:
Recall that a linear congruence $ax≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)$ has a unique solution modulo $n$ if and only if $\text{gcd}(a,n)=1.$

In the given congruence, we have $a=7$ and $n=30$, and

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(7,30)=1.
$$

So, our congruence does indeed have a unique solution.

To find the solution, we need to multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $7\,(\text{mod}\,30).$ To find the inverse of $7\,(\text{mod}\,30)$, we compute the exponents of $7\,(\text{mod}\,30)$ until we get a result of $1\,(\text{mod}\,30):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{7}^{2} & ≡49≡30+19≡19 &  & (\text{mod}\,30) \\ {7}^{3} & ≡19\cdot 7≡133≡4\cdot 30+13≡13 &  & (\text{mod}\,30) \\ {7}^{4} & ≡13\cdot 7≡91≡3\cdot 30+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,30)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $13\cdot 7≡1\,(\text{mod}\,30),$ which means that $13$ is the multiplicative inverse of $7$ (modulo $30$).

Now, multiplying both sides of our congruence by $13,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}7x & ≡6 &  & (\text{mod}\,30) \\ 13\cdot 7x & ≡13\cdot 6 &  & (\text{mod}\,30) \\ (13\cdot 7)x & ≡78 &  & (\text{mod}\,30) \\ 1\cdot x & ≡2\cdot 30+18 &  & (\text{mod}\,30) \\ x & ≡18 &  & (\text{mod}\,30)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x≡18\,(\text{mod}\,30).$
